title: China Reclaims Top Spot as Vietnam's Largest Tourism Source in Record-Breaking 2026
excerpt: Vietnam crossed 10.6 million international arrivals in five months, with China, South Korea, and a fast-rising India reshaping Southeast Asia's tourism landscape
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Vietnam welcomed over 10.6 million international arrivals in early 2026, its best start ever.
  • China is now Vietnam's largest tourism source, contributing over one million visitors in early 2026.
  • India's travel demand to Vietnam is growing rapidly, with rates exceeding 100% due to new air routes.
  • Vietnam's tourism strategy includes e-visa reforms and expanded connectivity, diversifying beyond major cities.

  • Vietnam recorded over 10.6 million international arrivals in the first five months of 2026, its strongest start to a year, with China emerging as the single largest source market ahead of South Korea.
  • China and South Korea together account for nearly 40% of Vietnam's total inbound tourism volume, with Chinese arrivals exceeding one million in the opening months of the year.
  • India has become the fastest-rising source market, with travel demand indicators showing growth rates exceeding 100%, driven by expanding direct air routes and affordable Southeast Asian itineraries.
  • Vietnam's e-visa reforms, expanded air connectivity, and aggressive destination diversification beyond Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City are reshaping Southeast Asia's tourism hierarchy.

Vietnam's tourism sector has entered what industry analysts are calling a structural transformation. The country recorded more than 10.6 million international arrivals in the first five months of 2026, marking its strongest-ever start to a year and positioning it to surpass the 21.2 million full-year arrivals recorded in 2025. At the centre of this surge is a decisive shift in the source-market balance: China has reclaimed the top position as Vietnam's largest single source of tourists, overtaking South Korea, which had temporarily led during the slower Chinese post-pandemic recovery.

China's Dominance Is Structural

Chinese travellers contributed well over one million visitors in the initial months of 2026, according to industry data tracked by Travel and Tour World. The recovery is tied to three factors: the return of organized group travel from China, improved aviation connectivity linking cities such as Guangzhou, Shanghai, and Shenzhen to Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, and Vietnam's geographical advantage as a short-haul destination from southern China.

China now accounts for roughly one-fifth of Vietnam's total inbound traffic. The effect is particularly visible in northern coastal destinations and border areas, where hotel occupancy rates have risen sharply. Many flight routes suspended during the pandemic have been restored or upgraded, with some secondary Chinese cities gaining direct links to Vietnamese coastal destinations for the first time.

The shift has reshaped on-the-ground services. In Da Nang, Nha Trang, and Ha Long, hoteliers and tour operators are adapting language services and payment options to cater to a renewed wave of Chinese group and independent travellers.

"Growth rates exceeding 100% in travel demand indicators underline India's rapid shift from an emerging to a core source market."

South Korea Remains a High-Volume Stabiliser

South Korea continues as Vietnam's second-largest source market, with consistently high arrivals throughout the year. Korean travellers dominate leisure flows into Da Nang, Nha Trang, and the island of Phu Quoc, where resort-based tourism aligns with Korean holiday preferences. The market is characterised by high repeat visitation, providing sustained rather than seasonal demand.

Together, China and South Korea contribute close to 40% of total inbound volume, reinforcing East Asia's central role in Vietnam's tourism economy.

India: The Fastest-Growing Market

India has emerged as one of the most dynamic contributors to Vietnam's tourism expansion. Growth rates exceeding 100% in travel demand indicators underline India's rapid shift from an emerging to a core source market. Expanding direct air routes, improved affordability, and strong interest in multi-destination Southeast Asian itineraries are driving the surge.

Indian travellers are increasingly choosing Da Nang, Phu Quoc, and Hanoi–Ho Chi Minh City circuits that combine leisure, cultural exploration, and short luxury breaks. The rise is strategically important for Vietnam because it diversifies its inbound base beyond East Asia.

Policy Reforms Fuelling the Boom

Three structural pillars support the surge: visa liberalisation policies including extended e-visa validity and broader visa-free access; expanded air connectivity linking Vietnam to Asia, Europe, and North America; and aggressive destination diversification beyond the traditional hubs of Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.

Phu Quoc has recorded one of the strongest growth rates in search interest, reflecting rising demand for island-based luxury tourism. Da Nang, Nha Trang, and Sa Pa are also capturing increasing international attention, signalling a shift from city-centric travel to distributed destination experiences.

Driving Factors Behind Growth
›E-visa reforms enhance accessibility.
›Expanded air routes connect Vietnam to Asia.
›Diversification beyond Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.
›Increased interest in luxury island tourism.

What It Means for Indian Travellers

For the Indian diaspora and travellers from India, Vietnam's growing accessibility and affordability make it an increasingly attractive alternative to Thailand. The expansion of direct flights from Indian cities, combined with Vietnam's simplified e-visa system, has removed much of the friction that previously steered Indian tourists toward more established Southeast Asian destinations. With India now among Vietnam's fastest-growing source markets, the country is actively courting Indian visitors with tailored tourism products and multilingual services.
